page: Microsoft Azure E2ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the EDSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon 8370C core with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The processor includes 48 KB L1d cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core.

This server includes 77 GB of local SSD storage and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. The x86_64 CPU architecture supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX, AVX512F, and AVX512_VNNI for vector and neural network instructions, alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI.

Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core capabilities but lower multi-core and memory bandwidth efficiency. Single-core stress-ng CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores rank in the average tier, supported by average single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression speeds. However, multi-core benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, fall into the poor category, reflecting the physical limitation of a single core. Memory bandwidth tests also show poor uncached read and write speeds, and database operations like Redis SET and Passmark database tests perform in the lower percentiles.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E2ds_v5 offers a high memory density per vCPU, making it suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing power. It is best suited for small-scale databases, caching layers, light text processing, and basic web serving where memory capacity is prioritized over high-throughput multi-core compute.
